name: Ethics of Technology
description: As cryptocurrencies like bitcoin and etherium overtake the imagination of the financial world as well as the public, the attention on blockchain (or digital ledger technologies generally), i.e. the technology underlying cryptocurrencies, is also increasing. Indeed, the number of use cases of blockchain technology, with its promise of decentralized, trust-less, peer to peer transactions supported by immutable record keeping in multiple digital “ledgers”, is expanding rapidly. Both public and private sector enterprises and institutions alike are now looking closely at blockchain technology to solve long-standing problems in a variety of diverse use cases going well beyond the financial services sector. In order to distinguish between what is perhaps just the “hype” from the actual promises of blockchain technology, the seminar will look at legal and ethical issues surrounding this technology, with the help of use cases in 2 or 3 fields such as agri-business, medical data management, and the music industry. It also looks at how blockchain is likely to affect broader issues of business ethics, especially issues of leadership, organizational structures and corporate social responsibility. Cryptocurrencies and blockchain use cases in the financial services sector are expressly excluded from the scope of this seminar.
prerequisites: No. However, reading the 1st item in the recommended reading list prior to the first lecture is highly recommended in order to get the most out of the seminar.
